import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/training_6.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first index column
    # Ensure schema matches target schema: ['air_store_id', 'dow']
    # Convert dow to integer explicitly to match target schema
    df['dow'] = df['dow'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target,
# we can union (concatenate) all source tables vertically.
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Optional: Remove duplicates if any (not explicitly required, but usually safe)
# The prompt does not mention duplicates in target examples, so we keep all rows.
# If needed, uncomment the next line:
# target_df = target_df.drop_duplicates()

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_11/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
